focus: Skyline from Best in Mons Mouton PlateauThe terrain all around you, with the paths of the Sun and Earth over the next 30 days from 2026-11-15✕NESW11°0° (flat horizon) Sun, visible 70% of the month (faded dots = behind terrain) Earth, visible 38% Sun nowWhy is the Sun so low here?The Moon's spin axis is tilted only 1.5° from the Sun's path, compared with 23.4° for Earth. So the Sun drifts no more than about 1.6° north or south over a year, and at the pole it just circles the horizon. A hill a few hundred metres high, kilometres away, is enough to block it, and crater floors that sit below the skyline in every direction never see sunlight at all. Earth wobbles above and below the horizon too (libration), so radio contact comes and goes.+2°−2°Latitude where the Sun is overhead, 2026–2028 (-1.58° to +1.59°)
